text:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding a community HF chat model and seeing token drift after HF->Redwood conversion. Tokens differ for inputs with NBSP and some Unicode ligatures. Repro attached below.
ravi: can you paste the minimal repro? I want to run a token-diff script.
maria: here — original HF tokenizer vs converted Redwood tokenizer output for the same input (short):
```
text = 'Price is 10\u00A0USD — e.g. café\u200D'
HF tokens: ["Price", " is", " 10", "\u00A0USD", " —", " e", ".g", " e", ".g"]
Redwood tokens: ["Price", " is", " 10", " USD", " —", " e", ".g", " caf", "e\u200D"]
```
Notice the NBSP shows up differently and the grapheme joiner moved. my suspicion: normalizer/pretok config mismatch (NFKC vs NFC) + byte-fallback ordering.
joel: pretty common. HF tokenizers sometimes apply NFKC by default in their normalizer pipeline depending on tokenizer.json. Redwood pretokenizer expects NFC unless we explicitly set normalizer. Did you check tokenizer.json (normalizer and add_prefix_space)?
maria: yeah — HF tokenizer.json has "normalizer": {"type": "sequence", "normalizers": [{"type":"NFKC"}] } and "add_prefix_space": true. Our conversion script currently leaves normalizer blank and sets add_prefix_space to false by default.
ravi: that explains the leading-space differences. add_prefix_space changes how BPE merges work for chat inputs. Also byte-fallback differences will split NBSP vs normal space differently. Quick diff I ran on 1k samples showed ~0.8% token-count deltas concentrated on non-ascii runs.
ci-bot: conversion-job-#452 finished — warnings: missing normalizer in converted config; fallback to platform-default (NFC). See /tmp/conv-452.log
lisa: question — could quantization or kernel selection in Redwood affect tokenization? i.e., does runtime do any token-level normalization?
dena: no, tokenization is upstream of quant kernels. Quant affects logits only, not token boundaries. Focus on conversion layer.
maria: plan: update conversion script to preserve HF normalizer (explicitly set NFKC) and respect add_prefix_space. Also harmonize byte-fallback ordering (unicode->byte fallback) to match HF behavior. I'll open a PR with test vectors.
ravi: can you add a small regression: diff tokens on a set with NBSP, ZWJ, ligatures, RTL samples? I can run a 5k prompt pass and produce token-diff histograms.
joel: for quick local check, run: 
```bash
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('hf-tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('café\u200D\u00A0'))"
# then load converted tokenizer and compare outputs
```
maria: thanks — doing that now. tagging @ravi for the regression and @joel for conversion test suggestions. I'll push the PR and include the failing examples in the PR description. :thumbsup:
ravi: sounds good. once PR is up i'll run the 5k sweep and post token-delta CSVs to the thread.
ci-bot: reminder: please link the PR to issue #ml-onboard-217 so the conversion test runs in CI.
